title: Classical vs Hannebauer · you White · French Winawer, exchange
event: Classical OTB · Oweide · vs Torsten Hannebauer (DWZ ~1950) · resigned after 20.Ng3+
logNote: Clean: 13.Qd4! the only knockout after 12…Nfd7?; saw it to Qxg7/Qxh8+, not to 16…Rxc8. Resigned after 20.Ng3+.

steps.name: 1 Opening
steps.title: After 7…Be6 · where the edge came from
steps.prompt: Replay your moves 8–10 on the board. Then decide which Black move gave you the most — not which of yours was clever.

questions.name: concession
questions.label: 1.2 Which Black move cost the most in the opening?

questions.name: bd6
questions.label: 1.3 What does 10.Bd6 take away from Black — and which later move needs exactly that?

steps.key:
Material: a pawn up. The c5 pawn is still yours, and Black has given up the dark-squared bishop for your knight.

Concessions: 6…Bxc3+ and 7…Be6 each cost Black about half a pawn — the same size. 6…Nc6 or 6…Nf6 would have won c5 back quietly; after the trade on c3 Black owns no dark bishop, and 7…Be6 (instead of 7…Nf6) still leaves c5 alone. 5…c5 itself was nothing.

Your side: nothing to find. 8.Ne2, 8.Nf3 and 8.Rb1 are the same size; 9.Bf4 is a hair behind 9.O-O and it does not matter. 4.exd5 is the same quiet choice as in game 2 (XbhWoWMi) — the extra did not come from move 4, it came from Black's moves 6 and 7.

10.Bd6 keeps the king in the centre. That is the move that makes 13.Qd4 work: g7 and h8 hang together only because the rook is still on h8.

steps.name: 2 To the last capture
steps.title: After 12…Nfd7 · White to move
steps.prompt: At the board you saw Qd4 and the hit on g7, and stopped at Qxg7 / Qxh8+. Write the line to the last capture, both sides. Then say what is left.
steps.key:
13.Qd4 Ne4 14.Qxg7 Nxd6 15.Qxh8+ Ke7 16.Qxc8 Rxc8 — eight ply, and the count is only true at the end: you give the d6 bishop and get the h8 rook and g7. An exchange and a pawn up with a queenless board.

It was enough this time because every stop along the way was already winning. That is luck in the method, not in the result: in XbhWoWMi the same stop (at your own capture) cost the game. Count to …Rxc8.

Faster? No. 13.Qd4 was the only move that ends it at once — 13.c4, 13.Re1 and 13.Nf4 are good but give Black a game. From here Black resigned after 20.Ng3+.

steps.name: 3 His best tries
steps.title: After 13.Qd4 · Black to move · play his four tries
steps.prompt: You stopped where the win looked safe. Now play what Black could have tried instead, to the end of each line.

branches.label: Ne4 Qxg7 Qxc3 Nxc3 Nxd6 Qxh8+ Ke7 Qxa8
branches.key: The zwischenzug for Black: 14…Qxc3 grabs a pawn with tempo on a1. Take the queen — 15.Nxc3 — and h8 and a8 both fall. The desperado costs Black the second rook as well.

branches.label: Ne4 Qxg7 Qc6 Qxh8+ Nf8 Bxc6+ bxc6 Qxf8+ Kd7 Qe7+ Kc8 Qc7#
branches.key: 14…Qc6 looks like a counter-attack on b5. It is mate: 15.Qxh8+ Nf8 16.Bxc6+ takes the queen with check, and the queen walks the king to c8. 14…Nf6 and 14…Kd8 are mate in two.

branches.label: Kd8 Qxg7 Re8 Nd4
branches.key: The king steps off the pin, g7 falls anyway and Nd4 joins with Nxe6 and c4 in the air. Worse than the game.

branches.label: f6 Bxc5 Kf7 Bd6
branches.key: 13…f6 guards g7, but the d7 knight is pinned by b5 and cannot retake: c5 is simply a piece.

steps.key: 13…Ne4 was his best. Every other move loses more or gets mated. The position after 12…Nfd7 was lost, and you found the one move that shows it — the work left is counting it to the end before you play it.

steps.name: 4 If he had found Bd7
steps.title: After 12.Bb5+ · Black to move · the defence he missed
steps.prompt: 12…Nfd7 lost on the spot. Play 12…Bd7 and White's best answer, then decide how much of the win was yours.

questions.name: lost
questions.label: 4.1 Which Black move lost the game?

questions.name: plan
questions.label: 4.2 After 13.Bxd7+ Kxd7 14.Be5 — Black's king stays in the middle. What is your plan for the next five moves?

steps.key:
12…Bd7! 13.Bxd7+ Kxd7 14.Be5 Nce4 15.Nf4 — White is clearly better (a bit more than two pawns' worth), the king on d7 has no home, d5 is weak, but there is no knockout. Your plan: Nf4 against d5, f3 to kick the e4 knight, then Qd4.

What lost: 10…Qc8 (10…Rc8 was the move) made it hard, 12…Nfd7 made it over. The game lasted 20 moves because Black blocked the check with the wrong piece, not because there was a faster win for you before that.

steps.name: 5 Log
steps.title: Tag the game by its lesson
steps.prompt: A clean game still gets a tag. Pick what it teaches, not the result.

questions.name: stop
questions.label: 5.1 At 13.Qd4 you stopped at Qxg7 / Qxh8+. Why was that enough here, and when would it not be?

steps.key: Tag clean. From move 6 on every White move was the engine's first choice or level with it; 13.Qd4 was the only knockout and you found it. The one thing to carry over: you found the move and then stopped counting at Qxh8+. The leak doesn't cost anything in a position that is already winning, and it costs the game when the position is level — so count to the last capture anyway.
